localization->neuropsychology:develops.note: Moves from matching functions to brain areas to systematic study of brain-injury cases.

localization->split-brain:develops.note: Applies the idea of functional localization to the two hemispheres.

neuron-doctrine->hebbian:develops.note: Neurons must be separate units before changes in connection strength make sense.

neuron-doctrine->molecular-memory:develo.note: Traces learning down to changes in individual neurons and synapses.

hebbian->molecular-memory:develops.note: Cellular studies of synaptic plasticity test Hebb's idea.

ethology->evolutionary:develops.note: Both treat behavior as shaped by evolution; the latter extends this to the human mind.

split-brain->cognitive-neuroscience:merg.note: Gazzaniga brings the split-brain method into this new field.

cognitive-neuroscience->affective-neuros.note: Applies lesion and imaging methods to emotion and decision-making.

evolutionary->affective-neuroscience:bri.note: Evolutionary views supply the origins proposed for basic emotions.

psychopharmacology->affective-neuroscien.note: Drug targets led researchers to study emotional transmitters and circuits.

neuropsychology->split-brain:develops.note: Split-brain patients form a special category of brain-injury case study.

constructed-emotion->basic-emotions:crit.note: Challenges fixed basic emotions with the view that the brain constructs emotions.

monoamine-hypothesis->dopamine-hypothesi.note: Both share the idea that a transmitter imbalance causes psychiatric symptoms.

law-of-effect->operant:develops.note: Skinner rewrote 'outcomes that please are kept' as measurable reinforcement.

classical-conditioning->behaviorism:deve.note: Watson took the conditioned reflex as the basic unit explaining all learning.

behaviorism->operant:develops.note: Skinner pushed behaviorism to its limit, analyzing only behavior and its consequences.

behaviorism->neo-behaviorism:branches.note: Keeps objective methods but adds internal variables such as purpose and expectation.

classical-conditioning->behavior-therapy.note: Wolpe's desensitization builds directly on conditioning and extinction.

operant->aba:develops.note: Applies reinforcement principles to real educational and behavioral problems.

operant->social-learning:reacts.note: Bandura rejects the idea that learning requires being reinforced personally.

neo-behaviorism->social-learning:develop.note: Tolman's expectancies and internal representations kept cognitive processes in Bandura's theory.

classical-conditioning->learned-helpless.note: Learned helplessness research began from conditioning and avoidance-learning paradigms.

conditioned-reflex->rescorla-wagner:deve.note: Explains association by prediction error instead of simple temporal contiguity.

taste-aversion->behaviorism:critiques.note: Taste aversion shows that learning has biological biases, so stimuli are not interchangeable.

behavior-therapy->aba:bridges.note: Behavior therapy and applied behavior analysis share learning principles but developed separately.

psychophysics->experimental:develops.note: Fechner's measurement methods gave laboratory psychology its techniques.

experimental->functionalism:reacts.note: James opposed breaking consciousness into elements and asked what the mind does.

experimental->gestalt:reacts.note: Gestalt psychology opposed building perception up from sensory elements.

experimental->memory-experiment:develops.note: Ebbinghaus was the first to apply the experimental method to higher mental processes.

memory-experiment->schema:reacts.note: Bartlett criticized nonsense-syllable studies as detached from real memory.

schema->cognitive-psychology:bridges.note: 'Schema' became a basic term in cognitive psychology.

functionalism->cognitive-psychology:brid.note: Both ask what the mind does rather than what elements it is made of.

cognitive-revolution->cognitive-psycholo.note: Neisser organized the new paradigm into a discipline and named it.

cognitive-psychology->heuristics-biases:.note: Applies research on cognitive processing to judgment and decision-making.

cognitive-psychology->connectionism:reac.note: Connectionism disagrees that the mind is serial rule-based symbol manipulation.

cognitive-psychology->embodied:reacts.note: Embodied views reject the mind as symbol processing detached from the body.

connectionism->predictive-processing:dev.note: Multilayer networks and error-based learning are the foundation of predictive processing.

embodied->predictive-processing:bridges.note: The idea of a perception-action loop enters predictive processing.

ecological-rationality->heuristics-biase.note: Argues that heuristics are often smart in real environments rather than flawed.

chomsky-review->radical-behaviorism:crit.note: Argues that the stimulus-reinforcement framework cannot explain the creativity of language.

individual-differences->g-factor:develop.note: Spearman continued Galton's measurement tradition with correlation and factor analysis.

g-factor->intelligence-testing:bridges.note: The g factor gives a theoretical explanation for the common variance in test scores.

g-factor->multiple-intelligences:reacts.note: Gardner rejects a single g and proposes multiple independent intelligences.

intelligence-testing->test-theory:develo.note: Large-scale testing led to systematic requirements for reliability and validity.

trait->factor-personality:develops.note: Factor analysis organizes trait words into a few dimensions.

trait->big-five:develops.note: The lexical hypothesis and factor analysis converge on five basic dimensions.

factor-personality->big-five:develops.note: The Eysenck and Cattell debate ultimately converged on five factors.

person-situation->big-five:bridges.note: The debate settled on 'both person and situation matter,' which revived the Big Five.

open-science->embodied:critiques.note: Several results showing that posture or expression affects judgment have failed to replicate.

flynn-effect->intelligence-testing:criti.note: Scores rising generation by generation show that IQ is not fixed by genes alone.

lexical-hypothesis->five-factor-model:de.note: Questionnaire samples validated the five factors that the lexical hypothesis suggested.

child-study->cognitive-development:devel.note: Moves from describing children to a systematic account of the structure of thinking.

cognitive-development->sociocultural:rea.note: Vygotsky rejected development as an individual's solitary construction.

cognitive-development->moral-development.note: Kohlberg extended Piaget's study of moral judgment into a stage theory.

cognitive-development->theory-of-mind:de.note: Understanding others' perspectives grew out of Piaget's problem of egocentrism.

cognitive-development->infant-cognition:.note: Experiments show infants have knowledge much earlier than Piaget thought.

psychosocial->lifespan:develops.note: Extends development from childhood to the whole life course.

ecological->lifespan:bridges.note: The view of individuals interacting with historical environments is shared by both.

infant-cognition->theory-of-mind:bridges.note: Implicit false-belief research tries to move the starting point of theory of mind earlier.

ethic-of-care->six-stage-moral-reasoning.note: Argues that the stage model treated male reasoning as the standard.

contact-comfort->behaviorism:critiques.note: Infant monkeys cling to a cloth mother without feeding, refuting the idea that attachment comes from feeding reinforcement.

sociocultural->ecological:bridges.note: Understanding development within society and culture; the two share this idea.

piaget-stages->zone-of-proximal-developm.note: The latter stresses that instruction can drive development rather than waiting for maturation.

social-identity->crowd:critiques.note: Shows that group behavior follows norms tied to group identity, not a loss of reason.

field-theory->conformity-obedience:devel.note: The idea of the power of the situation passed from Lewin to Asch and Milgram.

dissonance->social-cognition:develops.note: The idea that people seek inner consistency entered social cognition.

attribution->social-cognition:develops.note: Attribution research is the forerunner of social cognition's study of how people explain others.

prejudice->social-identity:develops.note: After contact research, people turned to asking how prejudice relates to group membership.

indigenous->cultural:develops.note: Doubts about the applicability of Western psychology drove research on how culture shapes the mind.

independent-interdependent-self->fundame.note: The bias is weaker in East Asian samples, showing that it is not universal.

weird-samples->social-cognition:critique.note: Many 'universal' cognitive findings come only from Western university students.

self-perception-theory->cognitive-disson.note: Explains attitude change without needing discomfort.

logotherapy->existential:bridges.note: The themes of meaning and choice become core issues in existential therapy.

person-centered->eft:develops.note: Empathy and following the client's experience become the starting point of emotion-focused therapy.

gestalt-therapy->eft:develops.note: Greenberg integrates techniques such as the two chairs and tests them empirically.

needs->sdt:bridges.note: Values growth needs but replaces the fixed hierarchy with three basic needs.

flow->positive:develops.note: Csikszentmihalyi is a shared advocate of positive psychology.

sdt->positive:develops.note: Autonomy, competence and relatedness become central to well-being research.

logotherapy->positive:develops.note: Meaning becomes one dimension of the model of happiness.

five-factor-model->grit:critiques.note: Argues that grit overlaps heavily with conscientiousness, so whether it is a new construct is doubtful.

overjustification->behaviorism:critiques.note: Rewards do not always strengthen behavior; they can weaken original interest.

terror-management->psychoanalysis:bridge.note: Turns Becker's psychoanalytic ideas about the denial of death into testable experiments.

psychoanalysis->individual-psychology:br.note: Adler left Freud's circle because he rejected the sexual-centered account.

psychoanalysis->analytical-psychology:br.note: Jung rejected the purely sexual reading of libido and broke with Freud.

psychoanalysis->ego-psychology:develops.note: Shifts from instinctual conflict to how the ego adapts and defends.

psychoanalysis->object-relations:branche.note: Klein moved the focus to early relationships with objects, away from drive theory.

psychoanalysis->neo-freudian:branches.note: Horney and Sullivan rejected libido theory and turned to culture and interpersonal relations.

psychoanalysis->lacanian:develops.note: Lacan claimed to 'return to Freud' and reread him through structural linguistics.

ego-psychology->self-psychology:branches.note: Kohut, starting from ego psychology, turned to the self and to empathy.

object-relations->relational:merges.note: Object relations is one of the main sources of the relational school.

neo-freudian->relational:merges.note: Sullivan's interpersonal psychoanalysis is one of the sources of the relational school.

analytical-psychology->post-jungian:deve.note: Post-Jungian scholars carry on and revise Jung's theories.

dissociation->analytical-psychology:brid.note: Jung's concept of the complex drew on Janet's idea of dissociation.

five-factor-model->psychological-types:c.note: Personality differences are mostly continuous, not either-or types.

misinformation-effect->repression:critiq.note: Experiments show memories can be rewritten by suggestion, undermining the idea that repressed memories can be recovered intact.

relational->mentalization:bridges.note: Both stress the role of understanding others' mental states within relationships.

clinical-psychology->common-factors:brid.note: Professional assessment and help for individuals leads to the question of what actually works.

rosenhan-experiment->nosology:critiques.note: Accuses psychiatric diagnosis of being unreliable in practice.
